edges.effect_quant: Microbiome signals are usually more consistent for fermentation-related biomarkers than for broad clinical claims.
edges.mechanism: Caesarean birth may affect Childhood gut microbiome by changing substrate availability for gut microbes, altering short-chain fatty acid production, improving barrier function, or modifying immune tone. Microbiome endpoints are sensitive to sequencing methods, baseline diet, and host factors, which is why results can look heterogeneous across studies.
edges.summary: Caesarean birth appears harmful for Childhood gut microbiome in infants, but the confidence often depends on whether the endpoint is a microbial marker or a harder clinical outcome. Fermentation-based fibers and well-studied probiotic strains usually have the clearest signal, while broader microbiome claims stay more cautious. Overall, the evidence favors modest, mechanism-linked shifts rather than sweeping microbiome resets.
edges.caveats: Microbiome diversity is not automatically the same as clinical benefit. Strain specificity, background diet, and short follow-up can all limit generalizability, so mechanistic improvements should not be overstated when symptom outcomes remain mixed.
